description: Lorenz Curve for Effective Project Management by Office Solution A Lorenz curve is a graphical representation of the distribution of income or wealth within a population. It plots the cumulative percentage of total income received against the cumulative percentage of recipients, starting with the poorest individual or household. The further the Lorenz curve is from the line of equality (a 45-degree line), the greater the inequality in the distribution. The Lorenz curve is a graphical representation used to show the distribution of income or wealth within a population. It helps visualize economic inequality, making it easier to understand how income or wealth is distributed among the members of a society. Key Concepts: Equality Line: This is a 45-degree line that represents perfect equality. If every person in a population had the same income, the Lorenz curve would lie along this line. Lorenz Curve: This curve shows the actual distribution of income. It typically bows below the equality line, indicating that income is not distributed equally. Cumulative Shares: Cumulative Population Share: The percentage of the population, starting from the poorest. Cumulative Income Share: The percentage of total income received by that cumulative percentage of the population.
